newsitem.title: EGYPT: Arab states hail new Palestinian "intifada".
newsitem.headline: Arab states hail new Palestinian "intifada".

text.p: Arab states on Thursday hailed what they called "the intifada of the Palestinian people" and said a tunnel Israel opened in Jerusalem was part of a plot to destroy a Moslem shrine.
It was the first time in at least three years that the Arab League had used the word intifida, which means uprising, to describe clashes between Israelis and Palestinians in Gaza and the West Bank.

A statement issued after an Arab League meeting in Cairo, called by Palestinians in response to Israeli actions in Jerusalem, said: "The Council of the League hails the intifada of the Palestinian people, with the participation of its leaders, in intrepidly confronting Israeli repressive practices."
At least 33 Palestinians and 10 Israelis have been killed in the clashes since Wednesday.
The meeting, at the level of permanent delegates from the league's 22 members, said Israeli attempts to Judaise Jerusalem were a clear violation of Palestinian-Israeli agreements.
"These violations empty the peace process of content and the Israeli government alone bears responsibility for the serious consequences which will ensue," it added.

It said an Israeli tunnel near the Wailing Wall, on the southwestern edge of the Moslem sanctuary in Jerusalem, was likely to damage the nearby al-Aqsa Mosque, the third holiest site in Islam after the sanctuaries of Mecca and Medina.
Israeli officials have has said the archaeological tunnel has existed for years and does not affect the mosque. They said a second entrance to the tunnel was opened to give tourists greater access.

"The council...considers what is happening to be part of an Israeli Zionist plot to destroy the al-Aqsa mosque, set up the Temple of Solomon, obliterate Islamic Arab landmarks and create more facts which harm the legal status of Jerusalem," it added.
It called for urgent intervention to restrain Israel by the U.N. Security Council and by sponsors of the Middle East peace process -- the United States and Russia.
Palestinians waged a seven-year uprising against Israeli rule in the West Bank and Gaza Strip that ended with the announcement of an Israel-PLO peace deal in 1993.
